memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: By the seventh day God had finished the work he had been doing; so on the seventh day he rested from all his work. — Gen 2:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
After six days of creating, God rested on the seventh. But we must be careful here—God did not rest because He was tired. The Bible tells us clearly that the Lord never grows weary (Isa 40:28). His rest was not the collapse of an exhausted worker at the end of a long shift. It was the satisfied pause of a Maker who looked at His completed work and stopped, because there was nothing left to do.

In resting, God set a pattern for us. He built rhythm into the very fabric of creation—work and rest, labour and stillness. In our busy world, where we often measure our worth by how much we do, this is a gentle reminder that rest is not laziness. It is God's own design, and He Himself modelled it for us.

Yet there is a deeper rest here that points beyond a single day. The restlessness in our hearts is not fully cured by a holiday or a good night's sleep. Jesus invites the weary and burdened to come to Him and find true rest for their souls (Matt 11:28). In Him, we stop striving to earn what He has already given. Learn today to pause, to trust, and to rest in the finished work of Christ.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you struggle to rest, and what does that reveal about where you find your worth?
- How might building rhythms of rest help you trust God more?
- What would it look like to find your soul's rest in Jesus this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You yourself rested and invite me to do the same. Teach me to lay down my striving and to find true rest in Jesus, who has done all that needed to be done. Amen.
